speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. speaker: Doctor
text:

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the negative Lyme serology and the presence of fever with migratory arthritis, I need to evaluate for other systemic causes like reactive arthritis or septic arthritis. REQUEST TEST: Joint aspiration and culture of the left wrist.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Joint Aspiration Left Wrist: WBC >50,000 /μL (markedly elevated); Gram Stain: Gram-negative diplococci seen

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of Gram-negative diplococci in the joint aspirate is highly suggestive of Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection, indicating disseminated gonococcal infection. Given your sexual history and migratory arthritis, this aligns with the clinical picture. DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated gonococcal infection
